about: PolyPid is a Petah Tikva, Israeli biotech listed on Nasdaq (PYPD) developing D-PLEX100, a drug-delivery product that releases antibiotic at the surgical site over weeks to prevent surgical site infections after abdominal surgery. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises. Pre-commercial B2B medtech and pharma firm with no consumer profile. D-PLEX100 received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and is in a Phase 3 trial called SHIELD II.

Shinobi Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biotech working on engineered cell therapies made from induced pluripotent stem cells, aiming to produce off-the-shelf immune cells for cancer and other diseases. It is private and venture-backed, with a 2024 funding round. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

It sells to pain clinics and physical medicine providers and is venture-backed. B2B medtech brand with strong recognition among pain specialists.

Sudo Biosciences is a Carmel, Indiana and San Diego biotech developing selective inhibitors of the pseudokinase protein TYK2 for inflammatory and immune diseases, including topical and oral candidates for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial. B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its approach targets the TYK2 pseudokinase with highly selective inhibitors to treat autoimmune diseases with fewer side effects.

about: TMRW Life Sciences is a New York company that provides an automated cryostorage platform for IVF clinics and egg banks, with RFID tracking and digital monitoring of frozen eggs, embryos and sperm in the TMRW Platform. It sells to fertility clinics under storage subscriptions and is venture-backed. B2B healthcare brand with growing recognition among fertility providers and patients. Its platform serves many US clinics and can hold thousands of samples with automated alerts.

Clinical-stage biotech focused on microglia, the brain's immune cells, as a route to treat neurodegenerative disease. Pipeline includes VG-3927, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist aimed at Alzheimer's disease, and iluzanebart (VGL101), an antibody for the rare leukodystrophy ALSP. It has no marketed product and earns nothing from sales; money comes from investors and partners. Went public on Nasdaq (VIGL) in January 2022, and Sanofi agreed to acquire it in 2025. Purely science-driven with no consumer brand awareness, so a very unlikely sponsor.

Oxfordshire psychedelic medicine developer, spun out of the Beckley Foundation's research. Lead assets are BPL-003, an intranasal 5-MeO-DMT formulation tested in treatment-resistant depression, and ELE-101, an intravenous psilocybin candidate, plus work in alcohol use disorder. Pre-revenue, funded by venture rounds. In 2025 it agreed to combine with Germany-based ATAI Life Sciences, creating the Nasdaq-listed AtaiBeckley. Clinical-stage and science-led, with no consumer products, so brand visibility is minimal and sponsorship fit is weak.

Maker of organ preservation solutions and perfusion products used by transplant centres to keep donor kidneys, livers and other organs viable between donor and recipient. Its portfolio is built around the Belzer UW cold storage solution and related perfusion fluids, sold to hospitals, organ procurement organisations and transplant surgeons worldwide. B2B medical business with a specialist customer base and virtually no public brand awareness. Operates from the Atlanta area in the United States (the Georgia tag is the US state), with operations in Europe and Asia.

about: Molecular diagnostics company that develops genetic and epigenetic tests for urologic cancers, with a focus on prostate cancer. Customers are urologists and labs; revenue comes from test fees billed to patients and insurers, roughly $90 million annually. Founded in Belgium, now operating mainly from California, and listed on Nasdaq (MDXH). B2B healthcare brand, little consumer visibility.

Developer of DCVax, a personalised dendritic-cell vaccine platform; the lead product DCVax-L for glioblastoma (an aggressive brain cancer) showed a survival signal in its Phase 3 trial, and filings have been made with UK regulators. It runs its own manufacturing in the UK. Has no approved product or meaningful revenue and is funded largely by insider loans and share sales. Quoted over the counter (NWBO), led by CEO Linda Powers. Clinical-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

London-based gene therapy company developing treatments for kidney disease, using gene delivery designed to reach the podocyte cells of the kidney filter. Developer of prescription digital therapeutics, software that doctors prescribe to treat chronic disease. about: Basel-based biotech developing antibiotics against drug-resistant bacterial infections. Candidates include alpibectir, an oral drug aimed at tuberculosis in partnership with GSK, and BV100, an intravenous rifabutin formulation for severe Acinetobacter baumannii infections in hospitals. Spun out of the University of Basel and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange in early 2025. Pre-revenue, so cash comes from investors, grants and partnerships. B2B science business with no consumer brand, so a poor sponsorship prospect.

Specialty pharma whose product PEDMARK (sodium thiosulfate injection) was approved by the FDA in 2022 to reduce hearing loss caused by cisplatin chemotherapy in children, with a European version sold via partner Norgine. Customers are paediatric oncology centres. Listed on Nasdaq (FENC) and the TSX. Revenue is a few tens of millions of dollars. Small niche drug company with no consumer brand.

Clinical-stage biotech (formerly Celsion) developing IMNN-001, a DNA-based IL-12 immunotherapy delivered into the abdomen for advanced ovarian cancer and tested in the Phase 2 OVATION trial, plus the PlaCCine synthetic DNA vaccine delivery technology. Renamed Imunon in 2022 after dropping its older ThermoDox liposome heat-activated programme. Listed on Nasdaq (IMNN), with no product revenue and funding through equity raises. Small specialist drug developer with no consumer brand or public visibility.

Pharmaceutical formulation company developing and selling specialty and generic drug products, mainly for the US market, including complex 505(b)(2) reformulations, through its own US-facing commercial and manufacturing set-up. Customers are US wholesalers, pharmacy chains and distribution partners; revenue comes from product sales and licensing. Controlled by global investor General Atlantic, it listed on the Indian exchanges in late 2025. Business-to-business with little consumer brand awareness in India or abroad.

Late-stage biopharmaceutical company developing galinpepimut-S, a WT1-targeting cancer vaccine for acute myeloid leukaemia being tested in a pivotal Phase 3 trial called REGAL, and SLS009, a selective CDK9 inhibitor for blood cancers. No approved product and no sales, so it relies on equity financing and partnering. Listed on Nasdaq (SLS), with a small staff. Specialist oncology business with no consumer visibility and little interest in sports marketing.

Chinese biopharmaceutical company with commercial products including TPIAO (recombinant human thrombopoietin for low platelet counts), Yisaipu (an etanercept biosimilar), EPIAO for anaemia, and Cipterbin for breast cancer. Sells to hospitals across China and has licensed pipeline assets abroad; a 2025 licence of its PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody to Pfizer brought a large upfront payment. Founded in Shenyang and listed in Hong Kong (1530). B2B pharma without consumer branding.

India's largest contract development and manufacturing organisation for pharmaceuticals. It makes tablets, capsules, injectables, ointments and nutraceuticals for other pharma and consumer-health companies under their own labels, and sells some branded and trade-generic formulations itself, from large factories mostly in Haridwar in Uttarakhand and in Himachal Pradesh. Listed on the Indian exchanges since 2024, with revenue above INR 3,500 crore. Mostly B2B manufacturer, so little consumer brand recognition.

Pharmaceutical company whose product ZUNVEYL (benzgalantamine), a prodrug form of galantamine, was approved by the FDA in 2024 for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and designed to reduce the stomach side effects of the older drug. Customers are neurologists, care homes and long-term care pharmacies in the United States, where it launched in 2025. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX Venture (ACOG). Small commercial-stage company with no consumer brand and modest marketing budgets.

Biotechnology company developing Apitox, a purified bee-venom-derived drug candidate for knee osteoarthritis pain, positioned as a non-opioid, non-steroid alternative to current joint injections. It is linked to a Korean parent and clinical programme and listed in the US through a 2025 IPO (ticker APUS). Pre-revenue, with Phase 3 work ahead, so cash comes from share sales. Small specialist drug developer with no consumer brand and little sponsorship relevance.

Biotechnology company that makes plant-derived DNA tags used to authenticate goods and fight counterfeiting. Its DNA marking is used in textiles and cotton supply chains, with a growing business making synthetic DNA by PCR for therapeutics and diagnostics. Customers are brands, manufacturers and drug developers. Listed on Nasdaq (APDN), with revenue in the low tens of millions. B2B, but brands that use it may be known.

Clinical-stage biotech developing NE3107 (bezisterim), an oral anti-inflammatory, insulin-sensitising drug tested in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, and BIV201 (continuous-infusion terlipressin) for ascites linked to liver cirrhosis. Billionaire Carl Icahn is a significant shareholder through his investment vehicles. Listed on Nasdaq (BIVI), with no product revenue and funding from equity sales and investor loans. Small research company with no consumer brand, minimal public visibility and little marketing activity.

Biopharma company whose product DefenCath, a taurolidine and heparin catheter lock solution, was approved in 2023 to reduce bloodstream infections in dialysis patients, and which also sells the Neutrolin version in Europe. Customers are dialysis providers and hospitals, which buy the product directly. Listed on Nasdaq (CRMD), with a 2025 deal to acquire anti-infective maker Melinta Therapeutics. Specialty hospital product company with no consumer profile.

Critical-care company with CytoSorb, a blood-purification cartridge that removes inflammatory molecules, toxins and drugs during intensive care and cardiac surgery, sold in more than 70 countries through its German subsidiary and distributors. Also developing DrugSorb-ATR to remove blood thinners during emergency heart surgery. Product revenue is about $35 million. Listed on Nasdaq (CTSO). B2B hospital product with no consumer brand awareness.

Clinical-stage gene therapy company whose lead product REQORSA (quaratusugene ozeplasmid, delivering the TUSC2 tumour-suppressor gene in a lipid nanoparticle) is being tested alongside AstraZeneca's Tagrisso in non-small-cell lung cancer, and it also has early diabetes gene-therapy research, licensed from MD Anderson and Baylor. No revenue; funding comes from equity offerings. Listed on Nasdaq (GNPX). Small specialist biotech with no consumer brand.

Clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing gamma-delta T-cell therapies, including INB-100 for acute myeloid leukaemia patients receiving transplants and INB-200 for glioblastoma, using its DeltEx platform licensed from the University of Alabama at Birmingham, plus drug-resistant immunotherapy approaches. Pre-revenue and listed on Nasdaq (INAB), funded by equity raises and grants. Academic-style specialist science with no consumer profile and no marketing presence, so a poor sponsorship prospect.

Chinese biologics company based in Chengdu and listed in Hong Kong (2162). Its flagship stapokibart (CM310), an IL-4Ra antibody, was approved in China in 2024 for atopic dermatitis and is also pursued for chronic nasal polyps and asthma, with further antibodies in allergy and autoimmune disease. It sells through hospital channels in China and licenses assets to partners. B2B pharma, no consumer brand outside medicine.

Lyon-based clinical-stage company developing microbiome-based therapies built from pooled stool donations, treating the gut flora itself as a medicine. Lead product MaaT013 targets acute graft-versus-host disease after bone-marrow transplantation, with European regulatory filings and a distribution partnership with Clinigen for Europe. Listed on Euronext Paris (MAAT). Pre-revenue, so funding comes from equity, loans and grants. Specialist hospital product with no consumer brand or sponsorship profile.

Neuropsychiatry biotech whose lead candidate, roluperidone, targets the negative symptoms of schizophrenia such as lack of motivation and emotional flatness. It received an FDA complete response letter in 2024, a major setback, and has no commercial products or product revenue. Listed on Nasdaq (NERV), run by a small team near Boston, and dependent on equity financing and cost cutting. No consumer brand and no marketing budget.

Antibody discovery platform: OmniRat, OmniChicken and OmniMouse animals carrying human antibody genes, plus ultra-high-throughput screening (xPloration), which pharma partners use to find therapeutic antibodies. Revenue comes from licence fees, milestones and royalties from roughly 80 partners and hundreds of programmes. Spun out of Ligand via a SPAC in 2022 and listed on Nasdaq (OABI). B2B research tools business with no brand awareness.

Clinical-stage company developing pelareorep, an intravenously administered reovirus immunotherapy tested in pancreatic, breast and colorectal cancer, often combined with checkpoint inhibitors or chemotherapy. Corporate base in Calgary with a US presence, listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (ONCY). No product sales; funded by equity raises and partnerships. A specialist drug developer with no consumer visibility, so it is not a realistic sports sponsor.

Biotech developing ONP-002, an intranasal neurosteroid candidate aimed at treating concussion and mild traumatic brain injury, a field of interest to contact sports. It earlier worked on lantibiotic antibiotics and probiotic products and vaccines, licensed from Intrexon, but has narrowed to neurology. Pre-revenue, listed on NYSE American (OGEN), with a very small team funded by equity raises. Brand awareness is nil, though concussion treatment is relevant to motorsport and contact-sport safety discussions.

Kansas-based company that appears under a biotechnology and clinical trials classification, with a large funding event shown in late 2025 and a listed-company flag. The name suggests a life-science or animal-health business, but the input gives no information on products, customers, ownership or scale, and the name is shared with older animal-health companies. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Biotech developing PAS-004, an oral macrocyclic MEK inhibitor intended for neurofibromatosis type 1 and related tumours, after pivoting away from its earlier ketamine-clinic and neuropsychiatry plans and its legacy imaging and psychedelic ideas. It has no marketed product and no meaningful revenue, and relies on equity raises to fund trials. Listed on Nasdaq (KTTA), with a very small headcount. No consumer brand awareness, so not a natural fit for sponsorship.

Biotech built around Cell-in-a-Box, a cellulose-based live-cell encapsulation technology intended to deliver cancer-activating drugs locally to pancreatic tumours and to produce insulin for diabetes. Formerly known as Nuvilex. It has no product revenue and a very small staff, but a sizeable cash balance built up from equity financings, which it has also discussed deploying in other ways. Listed on Nasdaq (PMCB). Little consumer or media profile.

Clinical-stage biotech developing PRP, a combination of proenzymes derived from pancreatic enzymes, as a treatment for pancreatic, ovarian and colorectal cancers and as a way to prevent metastasis. Its programme has been in early-stage development for years with no approved product or revenue, funded by small convertible-note and equity raises. Quoted in the US over the counter and run from Melbourne. No consumer brand.

Holding company run from the Newark area by Howard Jonas, spun out of IDT in 2018, with stakes in drug developers including Cornerstone Pharmaceuticals (the cancer metabolism drug devimistat), other early-stage cancer and brain research programmes, plus legacy real estate and cash investments. Revenue is small and mostly rental income. Listed on NYSE (RFL). Pure investor-style entity with no consumer brand or public profile.

Late-stage specialty pharmaceutical company, a subsidiary of Scilex, developing SP-102, a dexamethasone sodium phosphate injectable for sciatica that would be the first FDA-approved epidural steroid injection if cleared. Went public in 2025 through a SPAC merger with Denali Capital Acquisition Corp. No revenue yet; funding depends on its parent and equity markets. Customers would be pain clinics and spine physicians. No consumer brand.

Canadian anti-infectives company focused on drugs for infectious diseases and biodefence, with a pipeline that includes ATI-1701, a tularemia vaccine candidate, and ATI-1801, a topical paromomycin cream for cutaneous leishmaniasis, much of it supported by US government defence funding. Listed on the TSX (APLI), pre-revenue with a small team. Customers are governments and health authorities rather than consumers, so no brand awareness.

Calgary-based company whose Crunchbase industries are given as biotechnology and health care, even though its name suggests energy. The input gives no description of what it makes or sells, who owns it or how large it is, and the name is shared by several unrelated companies. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Specialty pharmaceutical company with prescription products in ADHD, including Adzenys XR-ODT and Cotempla XR-ODT, and a paediatric portfolio including Karbinal ER and Poly-Vi-Flor vitamin and fluoride drops, much of it picked up through the Neos Therapeutics acquisition. Customers are paediatricians and psychiatrists prescribing through US pharmacies, and annual revenue is around $100 million. Listed on Nasdaq (AYTU). Prescription-only products, so little direct consumer visibility.

Dermatology company listed on the ASX (BOT) whose product SOFDRA (sofpironium bromide) gel was approved by the FDA in 2024 and launched in the US as a topical treatment for excessive underarm sweating. It sells through dermatologists and specialty pharmacy channels and has other skin disease candidates. Revenue is early. A consumer-facing launch campaign is possible, but it is a small drug company.

Green chemistry company that has developed enzymes capable of breaking down PET plastic and polyester textiles so they can be recycled back into virgin-quality material. Planned a first industrial plant in Longlaville, France, though it was postponed in 2024. Partners include L'Oreal, Nestle Waters, PepsiCo and Suntory in a consortium of brand owners. Listed on Euronext Paris (CARB). Known to sustainability audiences, little consumer awareness.

Specialty pharmaceutical company with injectable products including Ryanodex (malignant hyperthermia), Bendeka and Belrapzo (bendamustine for blood cancers), Pemfexy (pemetrexed), Barhemsys and Byfavo for anaesthesia. Customers are hospitals, oncology clinics and wholesalers, and annual revenue was in the region of $300 million. Was listed on Nasdaq (EGRX) and entered financial restructuring in 2025. B2B pharma with no consumer brand. Its products are mainly generics-style injectables and 505(b)(2) reformulations, and it was founded in 2007.

Company that developed epigenetic biomarker technology to estimate biological age and used it for life-insurance underwriting and wellness testing, later changing direction several times, including a combination with a rehabilitation clinic operator. Went public via a SPAC in 2022 (NYSE American: FOXO) and burned cash with very little revenue. No consumer brand awareness; financially fragile, so not a credible sponsor.

Italian cell and gene therapy company, spun out of the San Raffaele research institute in Milan, developing Temferon, an engineered blood stem cell therapy that delivers interferon-alpha directly to tumours, tested in glioblastoma and other solid cancers. Listed on Nasdaq (GNTA) as ADSs and funded through equity. No revenue and no commercial products; a specialist science business without consumer visibility or marketing spend.

Mumbai-based pharmaceutical group making branded generics, specialty and over-the-counter medicines in dermatology, respiratory and oncology, including the Candid antifungal powder and cream range popular in India and Ryaltris nasal spray. Sells in India, the US, Europe and emerging markets, with annual revenue above INR 12,000 crore. Founded 1977 and listed on Indian exchanges. Candid and other consumer brands give it solid brand awareness in India.

Vancouver company that makes rare cannabinoids through biosynthesis and sells them via its BayMedica unit, supplying natural-origin ingredients for dietary supplement, food and cosmetic makers, while also developing INM-088 for glaucoma. Customers are ingredient buyers and consumer-goods makers, so the brand is B2B. Listed on Nasdaq (INM), with revenue of only a few million dollars. Little public brand awareness. The company was founded in 2011 as a cannabinoid drug developer before pivoting to manufacturing.

Developer of electro-optic polymer modulators and proprietary Perkinamine materials for photonic chips, aimed at ultra-fast data transmission in AI data centres and telecoms. Commercial products and revenue are minimal, with funding from share sales. Listed on Nasdaq (LWLG) and located near Denver. Deep-tech B2B play with no consumer awareness, although it is followed closely by retail investors. It has said it targets 100 Gbps-plus per lane modulators and works with foundry partners to prove performance.

Chinese biotechnology and medical company listed in the input as being in the Pudong area, with a funding amount shown in yuan and a listed-company flag. The input gives no description of products, therapy areas, owners or scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Medical imaging company, originally from Paris, whose Cellvizio system uses a flexible confocal laser endomicroscopy probe to give doctors real-time microscopic images of tissue during endoscopy in the lungs, bile ducts and digestive tract. Sold to hospitals in Europe, the US and Asia, with revenue of about 10 million euros. Listed on Euronext Paris. Niche B2B medical-device brand with no consumer awareness.

Medical device company developing thin-film electrode technology for monitoring brain activity and ablating tissue in epilepsy and chronic pain, with a commercial and distribution deal with Zimmer Biomet. Products include the sEEG electrode and the OneRF ablation system, cleared by the FDA. Revenue is small, in the low single-digit millions. Listed on Nasdaq (NMTC). Specialist B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Nantes-based immunotherapy biotech whose lead Tedopi (OSE2101) is a neoepitope cancer vaccine in a Phase 3 programme for non-small-cell lung cancer, with antibody programmes in inflammation and cancer partnered with major drugmakers. Listed on Euronext Paris (OSE). Revenue comes from licensing and collaboration payments, with no product on sale. B2B science business with little consumer visibility. Founded in 2012 as a spin-out of Effimune, it has partnerships with Boehringer Ingelheim and Veloxis.

Late-stage biopharma developing HyBryte (synthetic hypericin activated by visible light) for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, plus SGX945 for Behcet's disease and RiVax, a ricin vaccine, funded partly by US government contracts. Revenue is tiny and comes mostly from grants. Listed on Nasdaq (SNGX) and based in New Jersey. Specialist drug developer with no consumer brand and no sponsorship relevance. The company has been public for decades and trades with a very small market capitalisation.

Nasdaq-listed company, formerly Synaptogenix (a small neurology drug developer working on bryostatin-1 for Alzheimer's), that pivoted in 2025 to raise capital and hold tokens of the Bittensor decentralised AI network. Revenue is minimal and its value depends on crypto holdings. No consumer products or brand. Crypto-treasury companies sometimes spend on marketing, but this one has little visibility. Headquarters are in New York, and the business is run by a small executive team with a treasury strategy rather than operating products.

Small clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing non-opioid pain products: Epoladerm (a diclofenac patch), Probudur (long-acting liposomal bupivacaine) and Envelta, an intranasal enkephalin analogue for pain. No product is approved and revenue is zero, so funding depends on equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (VRPX), founded around 2017. No consumer brand awareness and very little cash for marketing. Its lead programmes were licensed in from academic and private owners, and management is based near Philadelphia.

Neurodegeneration biotech (formerly Prana Biotechnology) whose lead ATH434 is an oral iron-modulating drug tested in multiple system atrophy, a rare Parkinson-like disorder with few treatments. Dual-listed on the ASX (ATH) and Nasdaq (ATHE as ADRs). No product revenue; it is funded by capital raises and Australian R&D tax rebates. Specialist science company with no consumer brand or sponsorship activity. The company was founded in 1997 as Prana and relocated its focus from Alzheimer's drugs to Parkinsonian disorders.

Cambridge-based biopharma developing improved formulations of existing biological drugs using its Arestat platform, including ultra-rapid and concentrated insulins such as AT278, and partnering with larger pharma for development and commercialisation. Revenue is partnership and licensing fees, with a small team. Listed on AIM (AREC). B2B drug-technology company without consumer brand awareness. Its technology aims to make biologics more stable, less frequently dosed and easier to self-administer for diabetes patients, with insulin pumps and pens as target devices.

Paris biotech developing BIO101 (20-hydroxyecdysone), a plant-derived oral drug aimed at age-related muscle weakness (sarcopenia), obesity-related muscle loss and Duchenne muscular dystrophy, after an earlier COVID-19 trial. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris, with US ADRs on Nasdaq. Pre-revenue and financially fragile. A small specialist company with no consumer brand. Its drug is based on a plant steroid hormone studied at Sorbonne University, where the company was founded in 2006.

Surrey-based liquid biopsy company (previously ANGLE plc) with the Parsortix system, which captures circulating tumour cells from a blood sample for cancer research and, in the US, an FDA clearance for use in metastatic breast cancer. Sells instruments and consumables to cancer research centres and pharma, plus lab services. Listed on AIM. B2B medical technology with revenue of only a few million pounds and no consumer awareness.

Life-science tools company supplying instruments and consumables, including Harvard Apparatus pumps and lab equipment, Warner Instruments, BTX electroporation systems and Hoefer electrophoresis products, to academic, biotech and pharma research labs. Revenue is about $100 million. Listed on Nasdaq (HBIO), based in Holliston, Massachusetts. B2B science brand with moderate recognition among researchers but none among consumers. It was formed in 1996 and sells through direct sales teams and distributors in North America, Europe and Asia.

Bangalore-based operator of the HCG chain of cancer hospitals, India's largest private cancer care network with around 20 or more centres, and also fertility clinics under the Milann brand. Customers are patients and referring doctors; revenue comes from treatment fees. Founded by oncologist Dr B S Ajaikumar and listed on the NSE and BSE. A recognisable healthcare brand in southern India with growing national presence.

Chengdu-based drug discovery services company built around DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DEL), which it uses to find drug-like molecules for pharma customers, alongside traditional screening and early-stage lab services. Customers are pharmaceutical and biotech companies worldwide, with revenue from fees and licensing milestones. Listed on the Shanghai STAR Market (688222). B2B science brand without consumer awareness. Customers include major global pharmaceutical companies, and the company has operations in the US and Singapore as well as China.

Biotechnology and health care company shown in Paris, with a funding figure of about $53 million and a listed-company flag. The name matches a maker of automated fluorescence microscopy and diagnostic imaging systems, but the input does not confirm products, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Clinical-stage oncology company with one platform: INT230-6, a mix of cisplatin, vinblastine and a penetration enhancer injected directly into tumours so that high drug doses stay in the tumour while sparing healthy tissue. It is in a Phase 3 trial (INVINCIBLE-3) in soft tissue sarcoma and has been tested in breast and other cancers. Public since a 2023 Nasdaq IPO (INTS); no product revenue and a small team. Specialist research company with no consumer brand and no sponsorship activity.

Quebec pharmaceutical group listed as a pharmaceutical company, with a Boucherville base near Montreal. The name suggests a contract manufacturing or services supplier to drug and health-product brands, but the input gives no description of its products, customers, owners or size. A listed-company flag and a late-2025 funding event are the only other data points. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Martinsried (Munich) immuno-oncology company that develops T-cell receptor (TCR) therapies against cancer, working from its in-house library of tumour-targeting TCRs and a platform for engineering them, and has partnered with larger pharma on cell therapies.
